hypothesis: If Darwin's generalization holds, then among mammal species whose present-natural range includes any oceanic island more than about 300 miles (~483 km) from a continent or large continental island, essentially none are native, non-volant, non-marine terrestrial mammals.
pass_criterion: Using the PHYLACINE 1.2.1 present-natural range rasters (96.5 km grid cells), restrict to non-flying, non-marine species. Define remote islands as land cells whose nearest distance to a continental landmass or to a continental island of at least about 100,000 km2 exceeds 483 km. At most 3 non-volant terrestrial species (under 1% of the non-flying, non-marine set) have a native present-natural range on these islands, or every species that remains is a doubtful or human-associated record. In either case Darwin's claim, with his own 'free from doubt' hedge, is supported.
fail_criterion: At least 5 non-volant terrestrial mammal species (over 2% of the non-flying set) have a present-natural range on islands more than 483 km from a continental source. They must be endemic or indigenous, not known commensals such as Pacific rats, and have no record of human introduction. Examples would be native rodents on remote oceanic islands (Galapagos, Juan Fernandez, Hawaii, Mascarenes, Canaries) or native non-volant mammals on islands such as New Zealand. If so, the claim as stated is refuted.
interpretation: 'Terrestrial mammal' is read as any non-volant, non-marine mammal, so bats, seals and cetaceans are excluded. 'Continent or great continental island' becomes land of continental origin, and 300 miles becomes about 483 km. 'Domesticated animals kept by the natives' maps to the PHYLACINE present-natural range scenario, which removes human-mediated introductions by design. The dataset records gridded, IUCN-derived ranges, so the island test requires overlaying a distance-to-continent layer. The 96.5 km grid is coarse and may miss or merge small islands. Borderline cases such as Madagascar (about 400 km from Africa), New Zealand (only bats native), the Galapagos (rice rats) and Hawaii (only a bat) will be reported separately, and the Galapagos rice rats will be treated as a documented exception.

dataset.name: MegaPast2Future/PHYLACINE_1.2: PHYLACINE Version 1.2.1
dataset.why_it_fits: It is a public global mammal database. Its downloadable zip, PHYLACINE_v1.2.1.zip, is described by the authors as holding range rasters and a trait table, but I could not confirm the zip's contents from the Zenodo page. The planned fields are the habitat flags (Terrestrial, Marine, Freshwater, Aerial), Island.Endemicity and the present-natural range grids. These would let one select native non-volant terrestrial mammals and overlay them on islands by distance from a continent. Confirm the exact field names after downloading.
